subject: fennec
reasoning:
I'm planning the fennec fox model's proportions and basic scale, then sketching out the skeleton hierarchy starting with the root pelvis and spine chain.

I'll keep the API calls simple, leaning on joints and parts with explicit bone references rather than complex procedural chains to minimize risk of errors. I'm working out the spine as a three-point polyline chain from hips to chest, then continuing into a neck and head chain with similar logic.

Defining joint positions and parent relationships...

Now adding a jaw joint on the head, then building the front leg chains with shoulder-elbow-wrist-paw joints positioned symmetrically on both sides, parented to the chest.

Legs will be skinned using sweeps along each bone chain with tapering radii, capped with rounded ends, plus small box-shaped paws at the bottom—I need to check the paw's bottom edge doesn't sink below the floor plane.

For the hind legs I'm defining a digitigrade joint chain (hip, knee, hock, paw) with varying forward/backward offsets, giving the thigh a thicker radius than the lower segments. Now I'm thinking about how to construct the body itself—possibly lofting or sweeping along the spine.

For the body I'm setting up a sweep along the spine chain with varying radii at hips, mid-torso, and chest, matching the spine's length and extent, and applying a countershade paint so the back is sandy orange and the belly is cream.

For the head, I'm placing a slightly flattened sphere for the skull, a tapered cylinder aimed forward for the snout, a small dark sphere for the nose tip, and a cream-colored box for the lower jaw attached to the jaw bone.

Adding cheek fluff, dark eye spheres with highlights, and tear-mark details...

Now positioning the ear joints and shaping the outer ears with flattened cone geometry...

Computing the ear tip position from base plus direction gives a total height around 0.41, which feels too tall relative to a fennec's real proportions—so I'm scaling the ear length down to 0.13 and lowering the base to y=0.265 for better realism.

Now I'm setting up the ear-generating function for both sides, positioning the cone pivot at the center between base and tip, with a slightly dark rim near the tip. Then I'm building a tail chain from the hips back through four joints, tapering the sweep radius to create a bushy look with a darker tip gradient.

Writing the paint function for the tail's shaded underside, then settling on the final palette: sandy tan for the coat, cream for the belly, dark brown for the tip, and soft pink accents. Now I'm adding a chest fluff element as a cream-colored sphere at the front.

Sketching the head sphere, snout cone, and eye placement, calculating surface positions and offsets to keep features sitting naturally against the head geometry.

Now I'm adding cheek fluff cones angled outward and down from the face, plus a small jaw box positioned beneath the snout, adjusting the vertical placement so the jaw sits cleanly below the snout cylinder rather than overlapping it. I'm also confirming joint parenting uses the hips reference, then moving on to set hind leg paw positions further back along the z-axis.

Now I'm setting front and hind leg x-offsets with left/right sign conventions and naming joints by side suffix, assigning chain roles for the legs, tail, spine, and neck, then finalizing the metadata export.
